g9-history-uh3-t1.overview: Languages, Religions and Peoples of Ethiopia and the Horn sits inside Peoples and States in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of the 13th Century. Peoples and states of Ethiopia and the Horn open Unit 3 of Grade 9 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it introduces the language families and the settlement of the region’s peoples. Then it surveys the major religions: indigenous belief, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Next, it studies the pre-Aksumite states such as Punt, Yeha, and Damat. Also, it follows the Aksumite kingdom and the Zagwe dynasty of Lalibela. Finally, it reaches the Sultanate of Shewa and the rise of Ifat. Students will also learn how these peoples and states shaped Ethiopian identity today.
objectives: Differentiate the main language families of Ethiopia and the Horn.
Describe the major religions and how Christianity and Islam arrived.
Analyse the achievements of the pre-Aksumite and Aksumite kingdoms.
Evaluate the peoples and states of Ethiopia to the 13th century.
Discuss the success and failure of the Zagwe dynasty.
g9-history-uh3-t1.simple:
Languages, Religions and Peoples of Ethiopia and the Horn in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the Afro-Asiatic and Nilo-Saharan superfamilies of the region’s languages.
  • Then the major religions: indigenous faith, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
  • Also the settlement patterns of the many peoples and states of the region.
g9-history-uh3-t1.detailed:

Then the major religions: indigenous faith, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Also the settlement patterns of the many peoples and states of the region.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe the major religions and how Christianity and Islam arrived.
  • Analyse the achievements of the pre-Aksumite and Aksumite kingdoms.
  • Evaluate the peoples and states of Ethiopia to the 13th century.
  • Discuss the success and failure of the Zagwe dynasty.
